items.title: Final Fantasy XIV preps for the Moonfire Faire while addressing load times on the Switch 2 version
Square Enix Deploys An Emergency Update To Fix Final Fantasy 14 Loading Times On The Switch 2
items.summary: Now you can die in your duty without worry
items.content:
The Switch 2 version of Final Fantasy XIV is great except for terrible load times. A new patch is here to fix that. Last night, the game underwent emergency maintenance to address a bug related to players’ screens going permanently dark during battle phase transitions in dungeons or when attempting to revive a K.O.’d player. It seems to have worked. Players are now reporting reduced loading times.

『FF14』Switch2版のロード時間が短縮。蘇生やクレセントアイルのロード時間はさらに短縮！

先ほどアップデートが配信され爆速で修正。ロード時間も爆速に。 #Switch2でFF14 https://t.co/qDbLoGl50c pic.twitter.com/i2qe8pFJCn

— はっち速報｜ゲーム情報・新作レビュー@Game8 (@Game8_news) August 7, 2026

There were also a couple of issues affecting Switch 2 players who use touch controls. Apparently, the game would mark players using touch controls in dungeons as inactive, removing them from the dungeon. There were also issues with touch control targeting in a Gold Saucer shooting mini-game. Both of those glitches have been addressed, as well. But while you can use the Switch 2 mouse controls to play FFXIV , it seems like the latest update hasn’t addressed the lag issues with doing so.

The emergency hotfix addressed a number of other problems not related to the Switch 2, however. You can check out the full patch notes here .

items.title: Outside Of A Loading Glitch, Final Fantasy 14 Looks And Plays Great On Switch 2
items.summary: The idea that you can play a whole-ass MMO on a Switch feels illegal
items.content:
You know that millennial meme about how the bigger the task you’re tackling, the bigger the screen it demands? Apply that to video games. The more complex the game—strategy RPGs, 4X games, MMOs—the bigger the system I need to play it on. So the idea that I can now play Final Fantasy XIV on my teeny, tiny little Switch 2, no matter how much Nintendo has beefed up its specs from the original, feels patently wrong and yet…it’s pretty cool.

Let me be clear: Technically, the game works like a dream. It’s a big-ass game, requiring roughly 120 gigs of storage to download, and I had to delete a few games to make space. But once I downloaded it, I had no issues logging in or playing. Graphically, I had no issues either. Water, fire, and fabric flow pleasingly and particle effects from my spells look exactly as I expect them to.

My character is on the Gilgamesh world in the Aether data server. It’s not the most congested world in the data center, but it’s my understanding that all worlds in the Aether server are pretty full. Yet in the multiple occasions I logged in, I had single-digit and low double-digit queues and waited maybe a few minutes at most to get in.

The real test came when I portaled into Limsa Lominsa, the hub-city where everyone hangs out. I teleported in smooth as butter, and it was the same for Ul’dah. Though my experience hasn’t suffered any technical issues, that’s not true for others. Across social media, players have been sharing videos of the screen fading to black and not coming back.

this raise time on switch 2 is a big no no 😭😭😭 #FFXIV #FinalFantasyXIV pic.twitter.com/pHpbq5y2xt

— EazyAsPiez is replaying ffxiv (@EazyAsPiezzz) August 4, 2026

According to Square Enix , this is a known glitch that happens:

When the screen fades to black during a battle phase transition or when teleporting to a different map in an instanced duty When the screen fades to black upon reviving after being K.O.’d in an instanced duty When the screen fades to black upon using Return or a shortcut in an instanced duty

They’re working on an update to get that fixed. I have the habit of putting my Switch to sleep every time I put it down so I know that when I come back, I can pick up seamlessly where I left off. That does not work for Final Fantasy XIV , and every time you do that you’ll be forced to sign in again. It’ll be hard shutting that bit of muscle memory off. (You can make quick trips to the home screen, though, and your game will remain connected.)

Beyond hanging around in the place that’s known for causing slow-downs on every device because it’s always just that crowded, I had no connection issues, even playing in handheld mode on a home wifi connection that’s frustrated me greatly in the past. However, I do not recommend extended play sessions in handheld mode for two reasons.

There are settings to declutter your UI so it’s streamlined for the smaller screen. But I’m an old-school MMO player who wants all my info in front of me at all times, which makes it really hard for me to play this game on the Switch 2. That elder millennial gripe aside, I’m seriously impressed at how well this resource-intensive game works on this console. I know people have been playing big games on mobile for a long time now, especially with the advent of cloud streaming, but I feel like I’m getting away with something by playing an MMO as pretty and beefy as Final Fantasy 14 on a Switch 2.

items.title: Square Enix details loading times issue with Final Fantasy 14 on Nintendo Switch 2
items.summary: Square Enix has identified a loading times issue with the just-released Nintendo Switch 2 version of Final Fantasy 14. The company says that “loading times may take longer than usual when screen goes dark within the content.” An update is planned to address the issue. It seems that the origin of the problem stems from entering “a content area while...
items.content:
Square Enix has identified a loading times issue with the just-released Nintendo Switch 2 version of Final Fantasy 14.

The company says that “loading times may take longer than usual when screen goes dark within the content.” An update is planned to address the issue.

It seems that the origin of the problem stems from entering “a content area while surrounded by a large number of characters”. Square Enix says that “in some cases, the data reloading and cache clearing processes required for safe rendering are taking an extended amount of time.” The upcoming update will further improve optimization.

The full notice regarding Final Fantasy 14’s Nintendo Switch 2 loading issue is as follows:

We have confirmed that in the Nintendo Switch 2 version, loading times may take longer than usual when screen goes dark within the content.

Our investigation has confirmed that when players enter a content area while surrounded by a large number of characters, loading times within that content take longer than usual from the moment they enter until they exit. When this issue occurs, the delay is particularly noticeable in the following situations:

Regarding this issue, we have confirmed that in some cases, the data reloading and cache clearing processes required for safe rendering are taking an extended amount of time. We have therefore further optimized these processes to ensure faster data loading even under similar conditions, and we are currently testing the updated program.

We are working to release an update as soon as possible to address this and several other issues, so we ask for your patience until the issue is resolved.

Final Fantasy 14 is up on the Nintendo eShop. We have information about subscription fees, a perk for Nintendo Switch Online members, and more here .

items.title: Final Fantasy XIV Coins Used for FFXIV Switch 2 Subscriptions
items.summary: You can only buy Final Fantasy XIV Switch 2 subscriptions and some other items with the new FFXIV Coins currency.
items.content:
Square Enix went over the new Final Fantasy XIV Coins currency used for things like subscriptions that the Switch 2 version of FFXIV and its expansions through Dawntrail are available. These will be purchased from the eShop. However, as the subscription will be waved for about a month after launch as the company ensures the MMORPG is running properly, that currency will only be used for account services and Online Store optional items at the moment. No Nintendo Switch Online subscription is required to play, though there is a perk for people who have one and are going through the game.

Square Enix didn’t explain what the exchange rate will be for FFXIV Coins on the Switch 2 in its announcement. It only noted that will be the way people will need to pay for things tied to real money in the MMORPG. When someone buys them on the eShop, they will be credited to a Square Enix Account. Those could then be used on Mog Station or to get things like mounts, cosmetics, Home World Transfer Services, Character Renaming Services, Fantasia, or Tales of Adventure in the Online Store . It also noted that, in order to be sure the currency shows in your account, someone would need to close the MMORPG after buying them and log in again.

The Nintendo Switch Online Perk doesn’t require any additional in-game actions or purchases. The bonus lets someone get another free Aetheryte as a free destination. This means one more place someone could teleport to without paying gil.

As a reminder, multiple versions of FFXIV are available on the Switch 2 at launch and don’t initially require a subscriptions to play. The base game is $19.99. There is also a Complete Edition for $59.99 that includes all expansions and Dawntrail. The Complete Collector’s Edition is $139.99 and goes up through Dawntrail and has all of the original collector’s edition items from the main MMORPG and expansions.

Final Fantasy XIV is available for the PS4, PS5, Xbox Series X, and PC, the Switch 2 version arrives on August 4, 2026, and the new expansion FFXIV Evercold debuts in January 2027.

items.title: Final Fantasy 14 Switch 2 Launch Is a Surprise Success With One Huge Catch
items.summary: Performance impresses on Switch 2, even as subscription issues frustrate
items.content:
Listen Thread 2 Add Us Add on Google Preferred Source Google News Link copied to clipboard By Willa Rowe Published Aug 4, 2026, 10:33 AM EDT News Performance impresses on Switch 2, even as subscription issues frustrate

Final Fantasy 14 could finally introduce a controversial feature to welcome new players Pokémon studio's new game arrives on Xbox Game Pass today Rust's major August update is concerning for solo players Final Fantasy 14's Switch 2 launch is going better than expected, mostly Final Fantasy 14 Sign in to your Polygon.com account Warriors of Light can finally explore Eorzea on the Nintendo Switch 2 . On Tuesday, Aug. 4, Square Enix finally released Final Fantasy 14 on the hybrid console-handheld. For the most part, players report that things are going pretty well!

This marks the beginning of what Square Enix is calling a one-month early access period for Final Fantasy 14 on Switch 2. During this time, players can enjoy everything the critically acclaimed MMORPG has to offer just as they would on any other platform. Square Enix will not enforce the game's subscription requirement during the first month on Switch 2. Regardless of whether you are a new or returning player, you can enjoy Final Fantasy 14 on Switch 2 entirely for free during the early access period.

There is a caveat to this good news. When the early access period does end, subscriptions will be required and there's a special Nintendo tax . Typically, Warriors of Light pay for a single subscription that works for all platforms the MMO is available on. The Switch 2 version of Final Fantasy 14 , however, will require its own subscription, even for those who have active subscriptions already.

To mitigate the extra cost, Square Enix is offering Switch 2 subscriptions at half price for players with existing subscriptions. Furthermore, players do not need a Nintendo Switch Online subscription to play the online game. The complete edition of Final Fantasy 14 , which includes all currently released expansions, is also on sale for a limited time at a discount of 30%. Though if you are just curious to try the MMO, start by downloading the free trial. Once you purchase the game in any way, you can't use the free trial without creating a new account entirely.

Even with all the extra hoops to jump through on Switch 2, players are reporting that the game is running very smoothly. Some Warriors of Light, eager to test out just how much the console can handle, went directly to the Limsa Lominsa Aetheryte Plaza, one of the consistently busiest locations in the game. In handheld mode, the Switch 2 was able to perform admirably in this rendering gauntlet. If performance was players' biggest worry before the Switch 2 release, today's launch has assuaged those concerns. Most reactions on social media are just sharing their awe that the game runs as well as it does.

That isn't to say the launch has been without hiccups. Some players are posting excessively long download times. While the game's 117 GB is nothing to sneeze at, waiting over a dozen hours for the download to complete seems excessive. Of course, this could be caused by individual network issues and not a platform problem. The biggest issue players are facing is getting the game to work with existing accounts.

There are already a couple posts on the Final Fantasy 14 subreddit asking for help troubleshooting the complex setup process on Switch 2. Hopefully these are just growing pains of launching the MMO on a new platform and Square Enix will sort it out soon enough. The game is technically still in an early access period on Switch 2. Players can follow a detailed guide on how to set up the game on Switch 2 on the Final Fantasy 14 blog .

Overall, feedback has been resoundingly positive for the Switch 2 launch. At the very least, it gives curious players who have never tried the beloved MMO a perfect reason to finally see what all the fuss is about before the Evercold expansion is released in January.

items.title: Final Fantasy 14 launches on Switch 2 today, Complete Edition is 30% off for a limited time
items.summary: Square Enix’s MMORPG comes to Nintendo for the first time…
items.content:
Square Enix’s MMORPG comes to Nintendo for the first time

Video Game News 4th Aug 2026 / 1:06 pm Posted by Chris Scullion Final Fantasy 14 launches on Nintendo Switch 2 today.

Following a poor 2010 release, Square Enix ‘s MMORPG was reworked and relaunched on PS3 and PC in 2013 as Final Fantasy 14: A Realm Reborn, where it was received far better by fans.

The game continues to enjoy a large following in the 13 years that have followed, and has been released on a number of formats over the years, including PS4 in 2014, PS5 in 2021 and Xbox Series X/S in 2024.

Now it’s Switch 2 ‘s turn to get Final Fantasy 14, with Square Enix bringing the game to Nintendo players for the first time.

As with other formats, Final Fantasy 14 includes a lengthy Free Trial version – which is around 117 GB in size – as well as Starter Edition and Complete Edition versions.

To celebrate the game’s launch on Switch 2, the Complete Edition is 30% off on the Switch 2 eShop until August 8, meaning it’s currently $41.99 / £31.49 instead of its normal price of $59.99 / £44.99.

Players who purchase the Starter or Complete Editions will get 30 days of play for free, after which they will have to pay a monthly subscription to continue playing with their full benefits. If they stop paying their subscription, their character’s progress will freeze and players won’t be able to drop down to the Free Trial version.

Newcomers, then, may wish to start with the Free Trial, which lets them play through the entirety of the base game A Realm Reborn as well as its first three story expansions – Heavensward, Stormblood and Shadowbringers – entirely free with no subscription cost.

The Free Trial does have restrictions, which mainly involve interacting with other players. This includes Party Finder, Chat, Chat Groups, registering friends, Free Companies, trading, the Market Board and the Moogle Delivery service.

Players are capped at level 80 (instead of level 100) and have access to 18 playable jobs instead of 22. They also can’t take part in Ultimate Raids, PvP content or housing features.

Other than the above, however, the game and its first three expansions are fully playable with the Free Trial, meaning players who simply wish to play through the story should be able to do so free of charge.

items.title: PSA: Final Fantasy 14 Is Out Now On Nintendo Switch 2 But You Don't Have To Buy It To Play
items.summary: Hope you have that meme memorized because it's relevant again; something something free trial something something
items.content:
By now, if you’re a Final Fantasy XIV player, you’re sick of the copypasta that starts, “ Have you heard of the critically acclaimed MMORPG Final Fantasy XIV ? ” But loathe as I am to invoke a meme that’s long, long been run into the ground…it’s actually relevant again. Final Fantasy XIV is out on the Nintendo Switch 2 today. And if you’re one of the folks interested in trying the critically acclaimed MMORPG on the go, you may be tempted to buy one of the versions that’s now on sale at 30 percent off.

But you shouldn’t. Because, as the meme is so fond of reminding us, there’s a free trial available . And over the years, as the game has grown through expansions, the free trial expanded too. Now, instead of just getting A Realm Reborn and Heavensward and being able to play up to level 60, you get access to Stormblood and Shadowbringers too, bringing the character level cap up to 80. The freebies also include access to all the job classes released with the expansions: Machinist, Astrologian, Dancer, Dark Knight, Red Mage, Gunbreaker, and Samurai.

After you’ve reached the end of Shadowbringers , the next purchase step is the Final Fantasy XIV Complete Edition which includes the latest expansions, Endwalker and Dawntrail . Once you purchase any license for the game, you get 30 days of subscription time for free before you’ll be forced to kick out money for a monthly subscription. Players who have an active subscription on another platform will have to buy a new one (at half price) for the Switch 2, and a separate license. But one perk of playing FFXIV on the Nintendo Switch 2 (and the Playstation 5 for that matter) is that you don’t need to pay for an additional online subscription to play like you do on Xbox .

The free trial does come with certain restrictions. For example, chat commands are limited, you won’t have access to everything in the online store, you’ll be allowed a maximum of 300,000 gil (in-game currency), and a big one— you won’t be able to create your own party but you can be invited to a party or join one in the dungeon queue. Check out the full list of what’s allowed and what’s not here to plan you free-trial trip through Eorzea accordingly.

Here’s the lineup of pricing: Starter Edition – $19.99 Complete Edition – $59.99 ($41.99 with pre-orders) Complete Collector’s Edition – $139.99 ($97.99 with pre-orders) Dawntrail Expansion (requires base...
items.content:
At the 2026 Final Fantasy 14 Fan Festival in Berlin today, Square Enix revealed the release date for the MMORPG on Nintendo Switch 2. It will be out on August 4, 2026.

That was just one piece of news we got today. Square Enix also unveiled a Final Fantasy 7 Remake Trilogy crossover raid series and more.

Square Enix today revealed brand-new information about Evercold, the sixth expansion for its critically acclaimed MMORPG Final Fantasy 14 Online, set to launch in January 2027 alongside new playable content, a Final Fantasy 7 Remake Trilogy crossover raid series, the Nintendo Switch 2 version release date and more.

An extended teaser trailer for Evercold was also revealed, providing a glimpse into the world of the Fourth and the adventures that await the Warrior of Light in the start of the Goddless Realms Saga story arc.

During the Fan Festival 2026 in Berlin keynote address, Producer and Director Naoki Yoshida revealed the first new job coming to Evercold: Bastion—a main tank that wields a pair of greatshields known as skyltborg—and unveiled a trailer showcasing the new job in action.

Details were also shared on several new features coming to Evercold, including changes to the narrative structure that will be implemented for the main scenario, field, and game system, allowing players more freedom to choose what area they complete first between various paths in the main scenario. Through Auto Content Balancing, difficulty scaling and enemy levels will adjust to the appropriate player level as they play through dungeons in their chosen order. Additionally, a first look was provided for Character Action Skins, a feature that lets players assign alternate animations to personalize existing General actions, such as Teleport and Warp, with support for additional skins such as job actions arriving in future updates. Character customization will also be expanded so players have more ways to make their character stand out, including a greater range of color options with the new color picker, the ability to fine-tune features such as eyes and lips, new elements such as eye shadow, and more.

Following the reveal of the EVANGELION – Ghosts of Desire alliance raid series in April, Yoshida unveiled a new teaser trailer and announced that acclaimed director and animator Mahiro Maeda will join the project as a special guest artist and designer. Throughout his career, Maeda has contributed to numerous acclaimed projects, including “Mad Max: Fury Road” (2015) as a concept artist and designer, and “EVANGELION:3.0 +1.0 THRICE UPON A TIME” (2021), where he served as director, concept art director, storyboard artist, art setting designer and key animator.

Joined on stage by Final Fantasy 7 Remake series Director Naoki Hamaguchi, Yoshida also revealed “Beyond the Lifestream,” a new Final Fantasy 7-themed 8-player raid series that players will challenge in Evercold. Both development teams are working closely together to create an exciting new raid experience for players.

Further, Final Fantasy 14 will launch on Nintendo Switch 2 on Tuesday, August 4, 2026, with pre-orders starting today on Nintendo eShop. To ensure server stability, there will be an approximately one-month free subscription period on Nintendo Switch 2. Whether beginning with the Free Trial, starting their adventure with the Starter Edition, or diving into the full story and experience with the Complete Edition, more players than ever before will soon be able to join together in the vast world of Final Fantasy 14.

An outline of the content reveals from the keynote address can be found below:

Finally, Yoshida revealed the Evercold Collector’s Bundle, which includes a collection of physical items: the Evercold Special Art Box, Expertly Crafted Reaper Figure, Ethos Metal Keychain, Köttr Mini Plush, and Tapestry of the Fourth. Also included is the digital Collector’s Edition, featuring three in-game items: the Crystal Skyltborg bastion weapon, Vallhallar Odin mount, and Entreat Crystal emote. More information regarding availability and pre-orders will be announced in the future.
